title: Cold Expanded Fastener Hole Standard for Cleanup of Damage in Pressurised Shell Structure
abstract: Establishes cold expansion as the declared standard for reworked fastener holes in pressurised shell structure, replacing the ream-and-oversize practice and giving the repair designer a substantiated fatigue credit to work with.

sections.reason: Rework of a fastener hole after a crack finding has been done by reaming to the next oversize since entry into service, which restores static strength but returns the hole to the same fatigue quality as the original. On structure that is already at half its design life this is why a blended finding tends to return. Fleet data on the forward fuselage shows repeat findings within four years at the same fastener row in one case out of three. Cold expansion is well established elsewhere in the industry and the programme had no declared standard for it, which meant every application went through a bespoke substantiation.
sections.description: A cold expansion standard is declared for reworked fastener holes in pressurised shell structure. The mandrel and split sleeve set is called out through the tooling reference in the standard practice, and the plate D5110113425482, clip D5110116963848 and splice plate D5110118833865 that make up the qualification coupon set are released as reference hardware for operator training. Fastener EN824462K5 becomes the declared interference fit item for expanded holes and the sealing washer PE170760-37 is specified where the hole passes through the pressure boundary. The standard gives the applicable diameter range, the minimum edge distance, the maximum number of expansions on one hole and the inspection required afterwards, and states that an expanded hole may not be subsequently reamed oversize. Zones 113 and 115 are called out as the reference application area in the worked example. The rework is detailed on drawings D51101142795 and D51101154586.
sections.effects: No mass change and no electrical effect: this is a standard practice rather than a hardware change. Interchangeability is unaffected because the fastener diameter does not change. The substantiated fatigue credit is the point of the change: an expanded hole may be given an inspection interval based on the improved detail, which is what allows a repeat finding location to be closed out rather than re-inspected. Structure repair manual content and the damage investigation standard practice both require update, and the repair design office must re-baseline any published repair that relies on the ream-and-oversize practice.
sections.embodiment_note: Declared from production at MSN T00184. For aircraft in service the standard is made available through an information bulletin rather than embodied; it applies the next time a hole in the covered area is reworked. Operators need the mandrel set and a trained operator before they may apply it.

type_data.production_impact: Declared from MSN T00184, no line stoppage
